observation.visible_scene: A roll of white paper towels stands upright on a white plate with a black rim. A large section on the upper-left of the roll is already soaked with a brown liquid that has run down the side, and a dark circular hole sits at the top center. From the top-right corner a white spout continuously pours a thin stream of clear liquid onto the upper-right edge of the roll.
visible_changes: The clear stream from the white spout keeps falling on the top-right rim throughout the excerpt, forming a brown wet patch there that spreads leftward toward the central hole.
The brown-stained area around and inside the central hole grows larger and more saturated as the clip progresses, partly obscuring the open hole seen at the start.
The pre-existing brown stain on the left side becomes glossier and darker, and the vertical drip running down the side extends slightly.
The plate, roll, and background remain in essentially fixed positions; no significant camera movement is evident.
outside_clip_unknowns: The identity of the brown liquid and of the clear poured liquid is not shown.
How the initial left-side stain was produced, and what happens after the excerpt ends, are not visible.
The source holding the white spout is outside the frame.
uncertain_details: Whether the clear liquid is water cannot be confirmed.
The apparent slight jitter of the frame is ambiguous between handheld camera motion and scene motion.
The brown patch on the top-right and the spreading toward the hole could be one continuous wetting front or separate stains; the frames do not fully resolve this.
